cards.front: What is the ESP32 and why is it popular for IoT?
cards.back: A low-cost **SoC** with a **dual-core** processor and **built-in Wi-Fi + Bluetooth/BLE** → single-chip path from sensor to cloud (no external radio). Rich peripherals, cheap, huge ecosystem (Arduino/ESP-IDF/MicroPython).
**ESP32**: connectivity (Wi-Fi/BLE built-in), cheap, prototyping. **STM32**: deterministic real-time/industrial control, rich peripherals (CAN, advanced timers). Match MCU to the job.
**Cortex-A** = 'Application', has an **MMU**, runs full OS (Linux) → gateways/phones/Pi. **Cortex-M** = 'Microcontroller', no MMU, **deterministic/low-power**, bare-metal/RTOS → sensors/end nodes.

cards.front: Which hardware unit lets Cortex-A run a full OS?
cards.back: The **MMU (Memory Management Unit)** — provides virtual memory & process isolation. Cortex-M lacks it (only an optional MPU), so it runs one program bare-metal/RTOS with predictable timing.

cards.front: Map Cortex-A / Cortex-M to IoT layers.
cards.back: **Cortex-M** → perception/edge (sensor, real-time control). **Cortex-A** → gateway/fog (runs Linux, aggregates, edge analytics, bridges to cloud). (Cortex-R = hard real-time, automotive.)
**C** = compiled→native, fast, tiny, deterministic → production/real-time. **MicroPython** = interpreted on-device, readable, interactive **REPL** → fast prototyping/teaching (slower, more RAM).
**Prototype in MicroPython** (fast, interactive) to validate, then **rewrite production/real-time firmware in C** for speed, determinism, and smallest footprint.
**2 wires** (TX, RX), **asynchronous** (no clock; agreed baud rate), **point-to-point**. Used for **serial debug** and modems (GPS/BLE/Wi-Fi/cellular).
**2 shared wires** (**SDA** data + **SCL** clock), synchronous, **many addressed devices** on one bus. Best for **many sensors on minimal wiring**. Speed: 100k–3.4M.
**4 wires** (**MOSI, MISO, SCLK, SS**) + per-device select, synchronous, **fastest** (full-duplex, tens of MHz). Used for displays, SD cards, high-rate sensors.

**Polling** = CPU repeatedly checks in a loop (wastes cycles, can't sleep). **Interrupts** = hardware signals the CPU → pauses to run a short **ISR** → resumes. Interrupts save power (sleep until event) and react fast.
Keep **ISRs short** — do the minimum (set a flag / read a register), defer heavy work to the main loop (long ISRs block other interrupts). Protect ISR↔main shared data (`volatile`).

cards.front: Mnemonic for choosing a serial bus?
cards.back: **I²C** = fewer wires, more devices (addressed). **SPI** = more wires, more speed (per-device select). **UART** = no clock, point-to-point (debug/modem).
